content.title: About
content.content: Quinoa Flour, Pre-gelatinized, Organic is a finely milled powder made from quinoa seeds that has undergone a pre‑gelatinization process, improving its water‑binding capacity and speeding up hydration in doughs. The product is certified organic, produced without synthetic pesticides or GMOs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Quinoa is an ancient grain native to the Andes, cultivated for over 5,000 years.
Pre‑gelatinized flour absorbs liquid quickly, making it ideal for gluten‑free recipes.
Organic quinoa is grown without chemical fertilizers, preserving its natural nutrient profile.
Quinoa contains all nine essential amino acids, providing a complete protein source.
The flour has a mild nutty aroma that intensifies when baked.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Quinoa flour provides about 14 % protein, including all essential amino acids, supporting tissue growth and repair.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Mineral rich
items.content: Contains magnesium, iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for bones, energy metabolism, and immunity.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: It raises blood sugar slowly, beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and phenolic compounds help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Quinoa allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to quinoa.

items.title: Saponin content
items.content: Saponins can cause mild stomach irritation in sensitive people; rinsing seeds before processing is recommended.

items.title: High phosphate levels
items.content: Excessive intake may affect mineral balance in people with kidney disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Quinoa flour is suitable for gluten‑free baking, pancakes, breads, muffins, and breading mixes. Thanks to pre‑gelatinization it can be mixed with liquids without long soaking. It can also be added to smoothies, yogurt, or used as a thickener in sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation. Discard if it develops a rancid smell.
